verified.claim: salesHistory has no public source in Texas because the state is non-disclosure
verified.why_this_one: It converts a roadmap item into a PERMANENT refusal, which is a stronger claim than anything else in the artifact and the only one that changes what we may say to a customer.
verified.method: Read the two cited statutes at source rather than accepting the citation.
verified.result: HOLDS. Gov't Code 552.149 excepts real-property sales prices received from a private entity by the comptroller or a chief appraiser from public-information disclosure. Tax Code 22.27 makes owner-provided appraisal information confidential, including a sale price voluntarily disclosed under a promise of confidentiality.
verified.refinement: The statutes close the appraisal-district path. The broader cause is that Texas imposes no mandatory sale-price disclosure at all, so in most transactions nothing is filed to begin with. The deed record carries the transfer EVENT; no public record carries the PRICE. The lane's framing was accurate.

verificationByThisSeat.posture: Seven of eight rows are the lane's research and are recorded as reported, not confirmed. Good enough to order work against, not good enough to quote externally. Anyone acting on a specific row verifies that row first. This is the same standing this seat applied to P-181 and P-182.

findingsThatChangeTheOrdering.A_ossf_and_permits_share_a_source: Texas counties generally cannot require building permits for ordinary single-family construction outside city limits, so in unincorporated Texas the OSSF permit is effectively the permit record. One acquisition serves two rails across the large majority of the state's land area. This is exactly the two-rails-one-build case the dispatch asked to have surfaced rather than buried in two rows, and the dispatch pre-registered it as a possibility.
findingsThatChangeTheOrdering.B_hoa_is_two_mechanisms: SB 1588's statewide TREC database answers whether an HOA exists, not what it restricts. Existence is a statewide one-time build; restriction text is a 254-county deed-records problem. They must not share a roadmap line.

rosterChange.why: salesHistory is not a capability gap. It is an acquisition that cannot be made lawfully from public record in Texas. It belongs as a declared permanent refusal carrying the statutory citation, in the same shape as the envelope family's R-2, not as backlog someone may one day pick up.
rosterChange.owed: A ruling to declare it. Any future price capability is a licensed-source commercial decision for the operator, not a capability build, and is out of this row's scope.

missionDefectFound.what: The dispatch said 'READ-ONLY... you touch no store... no repo writes' and separately required a close artifact under _inbox/.
missionDefectFound.lane_behaviour: CORRECT. It wrote nothing, filed nothing, ran no claim, and said so plainly in its return rather than silently half-complying.
missionDefectFound.consequence: p203-capability-roadmap never appeared in _catalog/lane_claims.json while the other three lanes did, so the fleet's own instrument reported this lane as never started. The integration seat initially read that as 'either it never started or it skipped the claim' and could not distinguish the two from outside. The lane's return distinguished them.
missionDefectFound.fix: The mission now carries a section stating that read-only means no PRODUCT-repo writes and that the lane still claims and still writes its artifact and close in doc_repo. Landed in the same commit as this close.
missionDefectFound.generalised: A read-only lane that leaves no claim and no close is invisible to the fleet. This matches the standing rule that even a read-only verifier gets the full compiled header and an explicit _inbox close path.
